mainTopic: Whether the parts of a מנחה are sanctified separately in a כלי שרת (רבי חנינא, רב and שמואל), and whether a קמיצה or a slaughter done inside the היכל is valid.
overview: This amud opens with the end of רבי חנינא's view: the flour, oil and לבונה of a מנחה become holy in a כלי שרת only together. The גמרא asks why, according to him, the עשרון and the לוג were anointed. It answers that they serve offerings with only one ingredient: the מנחת חוטא and the oil of a מצורע. Next, the גמרא shows from שמואל's comment on a משנה about blood bowls that שמואל agrees with רב: one part of a מנחה can become holy without the other. The גמרא then examines רבי אלעזר's ruling that a קמיצה done in the היכל is valid. It defends this ruling against a challenge from the פסוק 'וקמץ משם', explaining that the פסוק only teaches that the קמיצה may be done anywhere in the עזרה. Finally, it turns to רבי יוחנן's ruling that שלמים slaughtered in the היכל are valid. It begins a challenge from a ברייתא about כהנים eating קדשים in the היכל during a siege, and this challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי חנינא: neither part is sanctified without the other
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא finishes his ruling: the parts of a מנחה are sanctified in the vessel only together, not one by one.
steps.simpleTranslation: This one is not sanctified without that one, and that one is not sanctified without this one.
steps.whatsHappening: We are hearing the end of רבי חנינא's opinion, which disagrees with רב. He says the flour and the oil of a מנחה cannot become holy in the vessel separately.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רב said that flour placed in a כלי שרת becomes holy even before the oil is added. רבי חנינא disagrees: the parts only become holy when they are in the vessel together. The next steps test this view.

keyTerms.meaning: Holiness; here, becoming sanctified by being placed in a כלי שרת
A sacred vessel used in the בית המקדש, which makes holy what is put into it
A meal offering, made of flour, usually with oil and frankincense

phrases.english: This one is not sanctified without that one
phrases.notes: "This" and "that" are the parts of the מנחה, like the flour and the oil.

phrases.english: and that one is not sanctified without this one.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא זוֹ קְדוֹשָׁה בְּלֹא זוֹ וְלֹא זוֹ קְדוֹשָׁה בְּלֹא זוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבי חנינא's statement, which began before this section, against רב's view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The parts of a מנחה are sanctified in a כלי שרת only together, never one without the other.

steps.title: Why was the flour measure anointed?
steps.stepSummary: If flour is never sanctified alone, why was the עשרון, a vessel only for measuring flour, anointed to make things holy?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי חנינא, why was the עשרון anointed? It is only made for measuring flour, and flour is not holy without oil!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי חנינא. The עשרון holds only flour, so if flour alone cannot become holy, anointing it seems pointless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The vessels of the משכן were anointed so they could sanctify what is placed in them. The עשרון was among them, yet it only ever holds plain flour. Under רבי חנינא's rule it would never sanctify anything, which is the problem.

keyTerms.meaning: A vessel that measures a tenth of an איפה of flour
Was anointed (with the anointing oil), making it a vessel that sanctifies
Flour

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Chanina,
why was the tenth-measure anointed?
(But isn't it made only
phrases.notes: Some versions don't have the words in round brackets.

phrases.english: for measuring flour alone,
and the flour is not holy without oil!)

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי חנינא's ruling from step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חנינא's rule that flour is not sanctified without oil.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The עשרון only ever holds flour, so under his rule its anointing would have no purpose.

steps.title: For the sinner's meal offering
steps.stepSummary: The עשרון was anointed for the מנחת חוטא, which has no oil at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: For the meal offering of a sinner.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: there is one offering that is only flour, the מנחת חוטא, and the עשרון was anointed to sanctify it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא's rule covers a מנחה that has oil, where the parts must be together. The מנחת חוטא has no oil or לבונה, so its flour is complete by itself and can be sanctified alone.

keyTerms.meaning: A sinner's meal offering, brought by a poor person, made of plain flour without oil or frankincense

phrases.english: For the meal offering of a sinner.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Finds a case where the vessel is needed: an offering made of flour alone.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The עשרון seemed to have no use under רבי חנינא.
steps.terutzMaskana: It sanctifies the מנחת חוטא, which has no oil.

steps.title: Why was the oil measure anointed?
steps.stepSummary: The same problem for the לוג: if oil is not sanctified alone, why was the oil measure anointed?
steps.simpleTranslation: And the לוג, why was it anointed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same question about the vessel that measures oil.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By רבי חנינא, the oil of a מנחה is not holy without the flour either. So a vessel that only holds oil would also seem to have no purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: A measure for liquids; here, the vessel used to measure oil

phrases.english: And the log, why was it anointed?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same kind of challenge as step 2, now about the oil vessel.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חנינא's rule that oil is not sanctified without flour.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The לוג holds only oil, so its anointing would have no purpose.

steps.title: For the leper's log of oil
steps.stepSummary: The לוג was anointed for the oil a מצורע brings, which is not part of a מנחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: For the לוג of oil of a מצורע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: the לוג sanctifies the oil a מצורע brings for his purification, which stands alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just like the מנחת חוטא, this is a case where oil is a complete item by itself, not part of a מנחה. So רבי חנינא's rule does not apply, and the vessel has a use.

keyTerms.meaning: A person with צרעת, who brings oil as part of his purification

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי חנינא, the עשרון and the לוג were anointed for offerings that have only one ingredient: the מנחת חוטא and the oil of a מצורע.

phrases.english: For the log of a leper.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Finds a case where oil is brought by itself.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The לוג seemed to have no use under רבי חנינא.
steps.terutzMaskana: It sanctifies the מצורע's oil, which is not part of a מנחה.

steps.title: שמואל agrees with רב, based on a משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says שמואל also holds like רב, and quotes a משנה about which measuring vessels sanctify liquids and which sanctify dry goods.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל also holds like רב, as we learned in a משנה: vessels for liquids sanctify liquids, and dry measures sanctify dry goods; but vessels for liquids do not sanctify dry goods, and dry measures do not sanctify liquids.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns back to רב's side and says שמואל agrees with him. It brings a משנה to show this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה sorts vessels into liquid measures and dry measures. On its own, it does not yet prove anything about flour without oil. The proof comes from שמואל's comment on this משנה (next step) and the reasoning about the dry part of a מנחה (steps 9–10).

keyTerms.meaning: Vessels used to measure liquids
Vessels used to measure dry goods, like flour
Make holy, sanctify

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה itself does not mention רב or שמואל. The גמרא is using it to show that שמואל's view matches רב's.

phrases.english: And Shmuel also holds
like this view of Rav, as we learned:
Vessels for liquids sanctify the liquid,
and dry measures sanctify the dry goods,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין כְּלֵי הַלַּח מְקַדְּשִׁין אֶת הַיָּבֵשׁ,
phrases.english: but vessels for liquids do not sanctify the dry goods,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא מִדּוֹת הַיָּבֵשׁ מְקַדְּשִׁין אֶת הַלַּח.
phrases.english: and dry measures do not sanctify the liquid.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף שְׁמוּאֵל סָבַר לַהּ לְהָא דְּרַב, דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the questions on רבי חנינא and returns to support רב's side of the dispute.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל holds like רב, that flour is sanctified in a vessel without its oil.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל's comment on the משנה about liquid and dry measures: the blood bowls sanctify dry things, which steps 9–10 show must mean the dry part of a מנחה alone.

steps.title: Blood bowls sanctify dry things too
steps.stepSummary: שמואל limits the משנה's rule to measuring vessels and says the blood bowls also sanctify dry things, based on a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: the משנה's rule, that liquid vessels do not sanctify dry things, was taught only about measuring vessels. But the bowls used for blood do sanctify dry things, as the פסוק says: 'Both of them full of fine flour mixed with oil for a מנחה.'
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל explains the משנה from the last step. He says its rule covers only measuring vessels, while the blood bowls sanctify dry things as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה split vessels into those for liquids and those for dry goods. שמואל says the מזרקות are an exception: even though they are made for blood, the פסוק shows them holding a flour מנחה, so they can sanctify dry things too. This statement is the base for the proof that שמואל holds like רב.

keyTerms.meaning: 'They only taught this about...': a way of limiting a rule to a narrow case
Measuring vessels in the בית המקדש
Bowls used to collect and throw the blood of קרבנות
A dry item, such as flour

phrases.english: And שמואל said:
They taught this only about measuring vessels,
phrases.notes: He means the משנה from the last step, which said liquid vessels do not sanctify dry things.

phrases.english: but the bowls (for blood)
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets.

phrases.english: do make the dry things holy,
as it says: 'Both of them full of fine flour
mixed with oil, for a מנחה.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא מִדּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the proof from step 6 by quoting שמואל's comment on that משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The rule that liquid vessels do not sanctify dry things applies only to measuring vessels. Blood bowls sanctify dry things too.

steps.title: But a מנחה with oil is wet
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא מדפתי objects that the מנחה in the פסוק is mixed with oil, so it counts as wet, not dry.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא מדפתי said to רבינא: But a מנחה is a wet thing!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא מדפתי challenges שמואל's proof from the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק talks about flour 'mixed with oil,' so the מנחה in the bowl is moist. If so, the פסוק only shows that the bowls sanctify a wet item, which proves nothing about dry things.

keyTerms.meaning: Wet or liquid

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא מִדִּפְתִּי לְרָבִינָא:
phrases.english: רב אחא from דפתי said to רבינא:
But a מנחה is wet!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the proof שמואל brought from the פסוק in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's use of the פסוק to show that the bowls sanctify dry things.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The מנחה in the פסוק has oil mixed in, so it is wet. A פסוק about a wet item cannot prove a rule about dry items.

steps.title: The פסוק teaches about the לבונה
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers that the פסוק is needed for the dry part of the מנחה, the לבונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to him: the פסוק is needed only for the dry part of the מנחה, which is the לבונה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers רב אחא's question. He says the פסוק is teaching about the dry part of a מנחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The flour gets oil mixed in, but the לבונה (frankincense) stays dry. So the פסוק does teach that the bowls sanctify something dry: the לבונה of the מנחה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is needed only for...': showing what a source really comes to teach
Frankincense, the dry spice placed on a מנחה

phrases.english: He said to him: It is needed only
for the dry part in it,
(that is, the frankincense.
phrases.notes: The round bracket opens here and closes at the end of the next step. Some versions leave out this whole section.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לֹא נִצְרְכָא אֶלָּא לַיָּבֵשׁ שֶׁבָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing what the פסוק comes to teach
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק is about the whole מנחה, which is wet from the oil.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק teaches about the dry part of the מנחה, the לבונה, which the bowls sanctify.

steps.title: So שמואל holds one part can become holy without the other
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reasons that a dry part of a מנחה can only be sanctified alone if שמואל holds each part can become holy by itself, like רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you think שמואל holds that a מנחה is not holy until all its parts are together, how could you ever find a dry part of it? When everything is together, it is all wet because of the oil! So learn from here that שמואל holds this part can become holy without that part.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its proof that שמואל holds like רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose a מנחה could only become holy with all its parts together in the vessel. Then the flour would always be mixed with oil, and nothing would count as a 'dry part.' Since שמואל speaks of sanctifying the dry part alone, he must hold that one part becomes holy without the other, which is exactly רב's view.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if you would think...': testing an idea to show it cannot be right
'How could you find such a case?'
'Learn from it': stating a conclusion
'This without that': one part becomes holy without the other

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל's teaching about the bowls and the לבונה shows that he agrees with רב: each part of a מנחה can become holy by itself.

phrases.english: And if you would think that שמואל holds:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מִנְחָה קְדוֹשָׁה עַד שֶׁיְּהוּ כּוּלָּן,
phrases.english: a מנחה is not holy until all its parts are there together,
how could you ever find a dry part of it?

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲלֹא כּוּלָּן לַחִים הֵן מִפְּנֵי הַשֶּׁמֶן!
phrases.english: Aren't they all wet because of the oil?!
Rather, learn from this that שמואל holds:
this part can become holy without that part.)

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ קָסָבַר שְׁמוּאֵל: הַאי בְּלֹא הַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רבינא's answer to finish the proof begun in step 6.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: שמואל holds that one part of a מנחה can become holy without the other, like רב.

steps.title: Compared to blood, a מנחה counts as dry
steps.stepSummary: A second answer to רב אחא: next to blood, even a מנחה mixed with oil counts as dry.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or if you want, say: compared to blood, a מנחה counts as a dry thing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer to רב אחא's question from step 8.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no need to say the פסוק is about the לבונה. A bowl is made for blood, and next to blood, flour mixed with oil counts as dry. So the פסוק itself shows that the bowls sanctify dry things.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if you want, say...': introduces another answer
Compared to, relative to
It counts as dry

steps.confusionAlert: This answer does not say a מנחה with oil is fully dry. It says it counts as dry only when compared to blood.

phrases.english: And if you want, say:
a מנחה, compared to blood,
counts as a dry thing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the קשיא of step 8 and offers a different answer from the one in step 9.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A מנחה mixed with oil counts as wet, so the פסוק proves nothing about dry things.
steps.terutzMaskana: Compared to blood, a מנחה counts as dry, so the פסוק shows the bowls sanctify dry things.

steps.title: A handful taken inside the Sanctuary is valid
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר rules that a מנחה whose קמיצה was done in the היכל is כשרה. He learns it from the בזיכין, which are removed in the היכל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Back to the statement itself: רבי אלעזר said that if a כהן took the handful from a מנחה inside the היכל, the מנחה is still valid. We see this from the bowls of לבונה, which are removed inside the היכל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to a statement of רבי אלעזר and quotes it in full so it can examine it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the קמיצה is done in the עזרה, but רבי אלעזר says doing it in the more holy היכל does not ruin the מנחה. His proof is the removal of the בזיכין from the שולחן, which happens in the היכל and permits the לחם הפנים to be eaten. Taking the קמיצה does the same job for the rest of the מנחה.

keyTerms.meaning: "The matter itself." The גמרא is going back to examine a statement it mentioned earlier.
Taking a handful from a מנחה to burn on the מזבח
The Sanctuary building, holier than the courtyard
The two bowls of לבונה placed on the שולחן next to the לחם הפנים
Valid

phrases.english: The matter itself:
Rabbi Elazar said:
A meal offering whose handful was taken in the Sanctuary is valid,
for so we find with the removal of the bowls.
phrases.notes: Removing the bowls of לבונה happens in the היכל and permits the לחם הפנים, just like the handful permits the rest of the מנחה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the שמואל discussion and returns to a statement of רבי אלעזר mentioned earlier.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A קמיצה done inside the היכל is valid, learned from the removal of the בזיכין in the היכל.

steps.title: A ברייתא says the handful is taken where a non-כהן may stand
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה challenges רבי אלעזר from a ברייתא. It reads "וקמץ משם" as the place where a זר may stand, which means the עזרה and not the היכל. The ברייתא also gives בן בתירא's different reading.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה objected: the פסוק says "and he shall take a handful from there," which means from the place where a non-כהן may stand. בן בתירא says the words teach something else: if the כהן took the handful with his left hand, he puts it back and takes it again with his right, "from there," the same place he already took it from.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה quotes a ברייתא that seems to limit קמיצה to the area where a זר may stand. That area does not include the היכל, so this contradicts רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A זר may walk in the עזרה but never in the היכל. If the פסוק says the קמיצה is done where a זר stands, it sounds like a קמיצה in the היכל is not allowed. בן בתירא uses the same words for a different lesson about the right hand. The challenge itself comes from the first opinion in the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-כהן
"The verse teaches": introduces the source in the פסוק
Left hand / right hand. עבודה must be done with the right hand.

steps.confusionAlert: The challenge to רבי אלעזר comes from the first opinion in the ברייתא ("where a זר stands"). בן בתירא's statement about the left hand is just the rest of the ברייתא being quoted.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya raises an objection:
"And he shall take a handful from there":
from the place where the feet of a non-priest stand.
Ben Beteira says:
From where do we know that if he took the handful with his left hand,
he should put it back and take the handful with his right hand?
The verse teaches: "And he shall take a handful from there":
from the place where he already took the handful.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי אלעזר's ruling from step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's ruling that a קמיצה in the היכל is כשרה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא limits קמיצה to where a זר may stand, which is the עזרה. That suggests a קמיצה in the היכל is invalid.

steps.title: The verse comes to include the whole courtyard, not to exclude the Sanctuary
steps.stepSummary: Either רבי ירמיה himself or רבי יעקב answers the challenge. The פסוק teaches that the קמיצה may be done anywhere in the עזרה, so we would not compare a מנחה to an עולה that needs the north side.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say רבי ירמיה both asked the question and answered it. Others say רבי יעקב told רבי ירמיה בר תחליפא: "Let me explain it to you." The פסוק is only needed to allow the whole courtyard. Otherwise you might think: an עולה is קדשי קדשים and a מנחה is קדשי קדשים, so just as an עולה must be done in the north, a מנחה must be done in the north too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רבי ירמיה's challenge, and first notes two versions of who gave the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's words "where a זר stands" are not meant to keep the קמיצה out of the היכל. They are meant to widen the area to the whole עזרה. Without that lesson, we might have compared the מנחה to the עולה, since both are קדשי קדשים, and required the north side. So רבי אלעזר's ruling still stands.

keyTerms.term: הוּא מוֹתֵיב לַהּ וְהוּא מְפָרֵק לַהּ
keyTerms.meaning: He raised the objection and he resolved it himself
"It was only needed for...": shows the true purpose of a source
The Temple courtyard
Offerings of the most holy level
The northern part of the עזרה, where קדשי קדשים are slaughtered

steps.confusionAlert: "Where a זר stands" sounds like a limit, but it actually comes to include more area, the whole עזרה. It says nothing against the היכל. Note that the 'north' reason given here does not hold up. Step 20 replaces it.
steps.whatToRemember: The answer is that the פסוק includes the whole עזרה rather than excluding the היכל. The reason given here, that we might have required the north like an עולה, is rejected in steps 15-19, and step 20 gives a different reason.

phrases.english: Some say:

phrases.aramaic: הוּא מוֹתֵיב לַהּ וְהוּא מְפָרֵק לַהּ.
phrases.english: he raised the objection and he resolved it.
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי ירמיה, who asked the question in the last step.

phrases.english: And some say:

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב לְרַבִּי יִרְמְיָה בַּר תַּחְלִיפָא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yaakov said to Rabbi Yirmeya bar Tachlifa:
I will explain it to you:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נִצְרְכָא אֶלָּא לְהַכְשִׁיר אֶת כׇּל עֲזָרָה כּוּלָּהּ,
phrases.english: it is needed only to make the entire courtyard valid,
so that you should not say:
since a burnt offering is of the most holy order,
and a meal offering is of the most holy order,
just as a burnt offering requires the north,
so too a meal offering requires the north.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: הוּא מוֹתֵיב לַהּ וְהוּא מְפָרֵק לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי ירמיה's challenge from step 13 and defends רבי אלעזר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the purpose of the source: it includes the whole עזרה rather than excluding the היכל
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק limits קמיצה to where a זר stands, so the היכל is excluded.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק only teaches that the whole עזרה is valid, not just the north as with an עולה. It does not exclude the היכל.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how a phrase that sounds like a limit can really be a widening. That keeps רבי אלעזר's rule about the היכל in place.

steps.title: A burnt offering is special because it is fully burned
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that a מנחה could be compared to an עולה. An עולה is כליל, completely burned on the מזבח, so it is holier in a way a מנחה is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about an עולה? It is special because it is entirely burned on the מזבח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions step 14's answer. Why would we ever have learned a מנחה from an עולה, so that a פסוק was needed to stop us?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 said we needed a פסוק so we would not require the north side for a מנחה, the way we do for an עולה. But an עולה has a special strictness: it is כליל, burned completely. A מנחה is not like that, so the comparison seems weak from the start.

keyTerms.meaning: "What about X? It is special because..." This formula shows that the source case has a feature the new case lacks, so we cannot learn one from the other.
Burnt offering
Completely burned on the מזבח

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not challenging the law that קמיצה may be done anywhere in the עזרה. It is asking why a פסוק was needed to teach that, since the comparison to an עולה would never have worked anyway.

phrases.english: What about a burnt offering? It is special in that it is entirely burned,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether the comparison to עולה that step 14 rejected was ever possible.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 14 that the פסוק was needed to block learning מנחה from עולה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An עולה is fully burned, which gives it a stricter status, so a מנחה could not have been compared to it in the first place.

steps.title: Learn it from a sin offering instead
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests we could have learned the north-side rule for a מנחה from a חטאת. A חטאת is not fully burned, yet it still needs the north.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn it from a חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to rescue the comparison by using a different source: a חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חטאת is not כליל, so the objection from step 15 does not apply to it. It still must be slaughtered in the north. So we might have learned from it that a מנחה needs the north too.

keyTerms.meaning: Sin offering

phrases.english: From a sin offering.
phrases.notes: A חטאת is not fully burned, but it still needs the north side.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 15 by switching the source from עולה to חטאת.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Substitutes a different source case that avoids the objection.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The comparison fails because עולה is כליל.
steps.terutzMaskana: A חטאת, which is not כליל, could still serve as the source for the north-side rule.

steps.title: A sin offering is special because it atones for כרת sins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects learning from a חטאת. A חטאת atones for sins that carry כרת, which gives it a special strictness.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about a חטאת? It is special because it atones for people who are liable for כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the new source. A חטאת also has a special feature that a מנחה lacks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חטאת brings atonement for very serious sins, the kind punished with כרת. That makes it stricter. A מנחה does not do this, so we still cannot learn from it.

keyTerms.meaning: Atones, brings forgiveness
People liable for כרת (spiritual cutting off) for serious sins

phrases.english: What about a sin offering? It is special in that it atones
for those liable to כרת,

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְחַטָּאת, שֶׁכֵּן מְכַפֶּרֶת עַל חַיָּיבֵי כָרֵיתוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Refutes step 16's use of חטאת as a source.
steps.kashyaTarget: Learning the north-side rule for a מנחה from a חטאת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A חטאת atones for כרת sins, a strictness a מנחה lacks, so we cannot learn from it.

steps.title: Learn it from a guilt offering instead
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests learning from an אשם. An אשם is not fully burned and does not atone for כרת sins, yet it still needs the north.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn it from an אשם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a third source, the אשם, which avoids both earlier objections.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אשם is not כליל, so step 15's objection does not apply. It does not atone for כרת sins, so step 17's objection does not apply either. Yet it must be slaughtered in the north, so it seems like a good source for a מנחה.

keyTerms.meaning: Guilt offering

phrases.english: From a guilt offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 17 by switching the source to אשם.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Substitutes yet another source case that avoids both prior objections.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Neither עולה nor חטאת can serve as a source.
steps.terutzMaskana: An אשם, which has neither special feature, could still be the source.

steps.title: All of them are blood offerings, so none can be compared to a מנחה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the אשם too, because it is a blood offering. Then it adds that this applies to all three, so the whole comparison to a מנחה falls apart.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about an אשם? It is special because it is a blood offering! And the same is true of all of them: they are all blood offerings!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the last source and shows that no animal offering could ever be the source for a מנחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אשם is an animal whose blood brings atonement, and a מנחה is just flour. That difference applies to עולה and חטאת as well. So a מנחה could never have been compared to any of them, and the reason step 14 gave for the פסוק is gone.

keyTerms.meaning: Kinds of offerings that have blood, meaning animal offerings
From all of them as well

steps.whatToRemember: A flour offering cannot be learned from any animal offering, because those are all blood offerings. So the פסוק cannot be coming to stop a comparison to the north side.

phrases.english: What about a guilt offering? It is special in that it is a type of blood offering!
And from all of them too we could not learn, since they are all types of blood offerings!

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְאָשָׁם, שֶׁכֵּן מִינֵי דָמִים! מִכּוּלְּהוּ נָמֵי, שֶׁכֵּן מִינֵי דָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Refutes step 18 and extends the refutation to every animal source, closing this line of reasoning.
steps.kashyaTarget: The whole idea, from step 14, that a מנחה might have been compared to animal offerings slaughtered in the north.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: All animal offerings are blood offerings, and a מנחה is not, so no comparison was ever possible and the פסוק was not needed for that.

steps.title: The פסוק stops us from limiting קמיצה to the southwest corner
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a new reason for the פסוק. The הגשה of a מנחה is done at the southwest corner of the מזבח, and we might have thought the קמיצה must be done there too. The פסוק teaches that it need not be.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the פסוק was needed. You might have thought that since it is written "and he shall present it to the כהן, and he shall bring it to the מזבח, and he shall take a handful," then just as the הגשה is at the southwest corner, the קמיצה must also be at the southwest corner. The פסוק teaches us that it does not.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the comparison to animal offerings failed, the גמרא finds a different mistake the פסוק comes to prevent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוקים mention bringing the מנחה to the מזבח and then the קמיצה right next to each other. That could suggest both must happen at the same spot, the southwest corner. The פסוק 'וקמץ משם' teaches that the קמיצה may be done anywhere in the עזרה. So the פסוק is not coming to exclude the היכל, and רבי אלעזר's ruling can stand.

keyTerms.meaning: It was necessary
You might have thought (the mistaken first idea)
Bringing the מנחה to the מזבח
The southwest corner of the מזבח
It teaches us

steps.whatToRemember: 'וקמץ משם' teaches that קמיצה can be done anywhere in the עזרה, not only at the southwest corner where the הגשה happens. It is not coming to rule out the היכל.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer keeps רבי אלעזר's ruling from step 12 alive, because the פסוק has its own job and does not exclude קמיצה done in the היכל.

phrases.english: Rather, it was necessary,
since it might enter your mind to say,
since it is written:
"And he shall present it to the priest,
and he shall bring it to the altar, and he shall take a handful,"
phrases.notes: "And he shall take a handful" comes from ויקרא 2:2. The גמרא reads the two together.

phrases.english: just as the bringing is at the southwest corner,
so too the taking of the handful must also be
at the southwest corner;
so it teaches us that it is not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 19 shows the comparison to animal offerings was impossible, this step gives a new purpose for the פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigns the purpose of the פסוק to block a different mistaken idea.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because the פסוקים place הגשה and קמיצה side by side, the קמיצה would have to be at the southwest corner like the הגשה.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'וקמץ משם' teaches that the קמיצה may be done anywhere in the עזרה. It does not exclude the היכל.

steps.title: Peace offerings slaughtered inside the Sanctuary are valid
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that שלמים slaughtered in the היכל are כשרין. The courtyard is only the lesser area, and it should not be stricter than the main area.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now to the statement itself. רבי יוחנן says: שלמים that were slaughtered inside the היכל are valid. The פסוק says "slaughter it at the entrance of the אהל מועד," meaning the courtyard. The lesser area should not be stricter than the main area.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a statement of רבי יוחנן that was mentioned earlier, and now looks at it on its own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק puts the slaughtering of שלמים at the entrance, which is the courtyard (עזרה). רבי יוחנן reasons that the היכל is holier than the courtyard. So if slaughtering is allowed in the lesser place, it must also be allowed in the main place.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter itself. The גמרא is going back to examine a statement quoted earlier.
Peace offerings
The Sanctuary building, holier than the courtyard
The secondary or lesser thing (here, the courtyard)
The main or primary thing (here, the היכל)

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule sets up the challenge that follows. If the היכל is automatically 'better' than the courtyard, why would anyone need a special source to allow things there?

phrases.english: The matter itself: Rabbi Yochanan says:
Peace offerings that were slaughtered in the Sanctuary are valid,
as it says: "And slaughter it at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting,"

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא יְהֵא טָפֵל חָמוּר מִן הָעִיקָּר.
phrases.english: and the lesser should not be stricter than the main.
phrases.notes: The 'lesser' is the courtyard and the 'main' is the היכל itself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion of the מנחה and the south-west corner, and returns to a statement of רבי יוחנן quoted earlier in the sugya.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שלמים slaughtered in the היכל are valid, because the lesser area (the courtyard) cannot be stricter than the main area (the היכל).

steps.title: A teaching about priests eating inside the Sanctuary during a siege
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן from a ברייתא. רבי יהודה בן בתירא looks for a source that כהנים may eat קדשי קדשים and שירי מנחות inside the היכל when enemies surround the courtyard.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא raises an objection. רבי יהודה בן בתירא says: From where do we know that if גוים surrounded the courtyard, the כהנים may go into the היכל and eat קדשי קדשים and the leftovers of the מנחות there? The פסוק says:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge רבי יוחנן. This step sets up the challenge, and the פסוק the ברייתא relies on comes in the next section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קדשי קדשים must normally be eaten in the courtyard. רבי יהודה בן בתירא looks for a special source that allows eating them in the היכל. This seems to show that the היכל is not automatically allowed just because it is holier, which goes against רבי יוחנן's reasoning.

keyTerms.meaning: The Temple courtyard
Offerings of the most sacred order, normally eaten only in the courtyard
The leftovers of the מנחות, eaten by the כהנים
The פסוק teaches. This introduces the source verse.

steps.confusionAlert: The full challenge is not finished yet. The ברייתא's פסוק and the גמרא's point come right after this.

phrases.aramaic: מֵיתִיבִי: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתִירָא אוֹמֵר,
phrases.english: They raised an objection: Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira says,

phrases.aramaic: מִנַּיִן שֶׁאִם הִקִּיפוּ גּוֹיִם אֶת הָעֲזָרָה,
phrases.english: from where do we know that if gentiles surrounded the courtyard,
that the priests may enter the Sanctuary
and eat the most sacred offerings and the leftovers of meal offerings there?
The verse teaches:

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתִירָא אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's rule from step 21 using a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's reasoning that the היכל is automatically valid wherever the courtyard is, since the lesser cannot be stricter than the main.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the היכל were automatically included, no special source would be needed to allow eating קדשים there. Searching for a source suggests the היכל is not automatically allowed.
